doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

title: The Basie band of the 1950s and 60s
summary: He knew the Wess, Foster, Royal, Newman Basie band best; recalls Lockjaw Davis's last playing.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: The Basie band over the years was one of your favorites.
Well they produced a lot of great musicians.
Yeah. Did you have a particular era of that group that you liked the most?

Well the one I knew the most was in the 50s and 60s with Frank Wess and Frank Foster, Marshall Royal, Joe Newman. That was the group that I guess I was most familiar with because that’s when most of the recordings were made that I had. They went on and there were other guys that came out of there, Lockjaw Davis for instance, last time I saw him
he was at a Gibson party. He’d had cancer and he’d been told never to play again. At the end of the party he grabbed his sax. And then he died.
